_about: The WATER LAYER's rules and looks (scripts/world/water_gen.gd generates from them; scripts/render/water_draw.gd and the board scripts/ui/boards/water_board_shot.gd draw from them). Track WB, 2026-10-10: a PROTOTYPE for the board variants/water/, NOT wired into the map. What is ALEX'S (decisions water-stepped-depth and water-layer, 2026-10-10): water is stepped colour washes in blue on the SAME height system as the land, with the same shadows; three depth steps (shallows, shelf, deep) at -3, -10 and -30 m ('Sounds good' to the lead's proposal); water is GENERATED from the seed like the rest of the map (the design doc's premise: an island, rivers running downhill to the sea, a road with a bridge where it crosses a river). EVERYTHING ELSE IS PROPOSED by Track WB: every number below carries _proposed. Record shape as in data/terrain/terrain.json ({value, _proposed, _reason}); keys starting with _ are documentation; scripts/world/terrain_data.gd reads it and test_water_gen proves that nothing in the file is unread. LENGTHS ARE METRES. COLOURS ARE ROLES, NOT HEXES: the water hue is new to the palette, so every colour is written as OKLCH numbers off the paper (lightness below the paper's, chroma, one hue) and resolved at load by water_draw.gd -- no hex in draw code (CLAUDE.md rule 6, docs/proposals/palette-architecture.md). SECOND REVISION (2026-10-10, after Alex: 'the seeds are too uniform. It looks like a big square of land'): the sea's SHAPE is now data too -- `shape` (a domain warp, the six archetypes, islands, inlets, lagoons), `cap` (the mask uplands fade into the sea by, read by the terrain at integration) and `quality` (the floors test_water_gen holds the shapes to).

salt._reason: mixed into the world seed for the water's streams (which edges are sea, the river's choices); water's randomness never correlates with the terrain's or the layout's

noise_per_m._reason: the large-scale noise that bends every coast, evaluated at the domain-warped position (shape.warp_m): a lattice every 1,100 m with four octaves (to about 140 m), so bays, headlands and spits are hundreds of metres to kilometres across

noise_weight._reason: landness L = base + noise_weight x (noise - 0.5) + terrain_weight x (terrain field - 0.5) - strength x sea bias + island lift; this moves a coast by about +/- 450 m

terrain_weight._reason: the terrain's own height field (the one the levels are cut from) shapes the coast at 30 to 250 m, so land and sea read as one relief

base_land._reason: L inland stays above zero (no inland lakes by accident); only a sea component or an island takes L through zero

strength._reason: the sea bias at its peak (1) takes L down by this; the coast is where the bias reaches base_land / strength, about 0.31

depth_per_unit_m._reason: metres of water per unit of landness below zero: about 6 m of depth 115 m out from a coast and 18 m about 350 m out, so the three steps are broad bands at the 0.35 planning zoom (1.8 x 1 km)

seed_offset._reason: sea noise seed = scene seed % 9973 + this (the terrain's is + 101)

adapt_shrink._reason: when a sea would flood one of the layout's sites, the sea's strength is multiplied by this (its coast pulls back) and tried again

adapt_steps._reason: how many times; then the last sea component is dropped, and if none is left the seed has no sea (a river only)

warp_m._reason: THE COAST IS NOT PARALLEL TO AN EDGE (Alex, 2026-10-10: 'the seeds are too uniform. It looks like a big square of land'). Every sea component and island is evaluated at a position pushed by a low-frequency vector noise this far (a field of up to +/- 900 m, typically a third of that), so an edge's coast wanders, a blob's outline is irregular and bays and headlands appear that no edge falloff makes

warp_per_m._reason: the warp's lattice: every 2 km, so the bends are kilometre-scale

reach_wobble._reason: an edge component's reach varies along the edge by +/- this share (noise), so even before the warp a coast leaves the straight

reach_wobble_per_m._reason: that variation's lattice along the edge: every 1.7 km

archetype_weights._reason: the seed picks one shape for its sea: coast (one wavy coast, perhaps an inlet), corner (two adjacent coasts round a bay), peninsula (sea on three sides, a tongue of land to the road's edge), bay (a big bay bitten into one edge, perhaps a second), islands (a coast with a few real islands offshore) or lagoon (mostly land, an inland lagoon joined to an edge by an estuary). Weights, not facts: the lead's brief asked for variety (some a peninsula, some a bay, some two coasts, some islands, some a lagoon)

reach_m._reason: a coast's edge reach: the coast lies about 0.69 x reach inside the edge (1,000 to 1,600 m)
each of the two adjacent edges' reach (the corner of sea is rounded by the warp)

side_reach_m._reason: the two side edges' reach: a tongue of land about 2.5 to 3.3 km wide runs from the road's edge

far_reach_m._reason: the far edge's reach: the tongue ends 1.6 to 2.1 km short of it

radius_along_m._reason: the bay is an ellipse of sea; its radius of influence along the edge (the water itself reaches 0.69 of it)

centre_in_m._reason: how far inside the edge the ellipse's middle is (negative: outside it, a half-bay)

turn_rad._reason: the ellipse is turned off the edge's direction by up to this much either way

second_chance._reason: the chance of a second, smaller bay on another edge

second_scale._reason: its size as a share of the first's

reach_m._reason: the coast the islands lie off is a broad sea, so there is room for them

count._reason: a few real islands, clustered, not every upland patch

radius_m._reason: an island's radius of influence (the land is about half of it: 160 to 550 m); the first is the biggest, the rest follow a falling curve

cluster_m._reason: the islands scatter this far round the cluster's middle

cluster_in._reason: the cluster's middle lies this share of the coast's reach in from the edge (deep water, off the shore)

min_sea_landness._reason: an island is only made where the sea is at least this deep (landness), and with open water all round it (the sea at its influence radius is at least a little below zero in eight directions), so it rises out of open water and is never a spit of the coast

peak_landness._reason: an island's middle stands this high above sea level (landness: 0.1 is a low island of a few metres, 0.25 has room for a hill)

min_gap_m._reason: islands are at least this far apart (influence radii not counted)

inland_m._reason: the lagoon's middle lies this far in from its edge: a map that is mostly land

radius_m._reason: the lagoon's radius of influence; its water is about half of it

peak._reason: the lagoon's sea bias at its middle (below 1: it is shallow, 30 m at most)

channel_half_width_m._reason: the estuary's water half width (its radius of influence is twice that)

channel_strength._reason: the estuary's sea bias at its middle: it is a shelf deep, not deep

channel_extra_m._reason: the estuary runs this far past the map edge, so it opens to the sea

chance._reason: the chance that a coast has an inlet: a narrow arm of sea run into the land from it

length_m._reason: the inlet's length inland from the coast

half_width_m._reason: its water half width (the radius of influence is twice that)

strength._reason: its sea bias at its middle

turn_rad._reason: it is turned off the coast's normal by up to this much

chance._reason: the chance that a map that is not an 'islands' map has one or two islands offshore

attempts._reason: a seed tries its shapes in turn (its own stream per attempt: a fresh draw of archetype and numbers) until one is dry round the layout and has enough sea; a sea is MOVED, not shrunk to a puddle. The first attempt is the seed's first choice (the survey's 'first try')

attempt_shrink_steps._reason: an attempt may pull its coast back this many times (adapt_shrink each) before it is given up on

min_share._reason: the least sea an attempt may leave, as a share of the map, for its kind: a map with a coast must have a real coast (not a puddle in a corner), a lagoon map is mostly land

site_tries._reason: a bay or a lagoon is placed at the best of this many seeded tries: the one farthest from the layout's keep-dry points

margin_far._reason: UPLANDS FADE INTO THE SEA. The terrain's height field is capped by a mask the water makes: an upland stands only where landness is above this margin (about 150 m inland of a coast), so no upland is a speckle on the water and none is a drowned plateau

margin_cliff._reason: ...except where a low-frequency noise says CLIFF: there the margin is this, and an upland runs to the very shore and meets the sea as a coastal cliff (the occasional cliff)

ramp._reason: how much landness it takes for the cap to rise from the first threshold to the field's top: about 150 m of coast over which the plateaus taper

cliff_noise_per_m._reason: the cliff noise's lattice: every 900 m

cliff_from._reason: the cliff noise's smoothstep: below this no cliff

cliff_to._reason: and at or above this a full cliff coast (cliffs are about a tenth to a fifth of a coast where there is an upland to make one)

floor_below_threshold._reason: the cap's lowest value is the terrain's first threshold less this, so capped ground is low ground (level 0)

grid_m._reason: the whole-map grid the shape measures (coast_stats) run on: 100 x 100 samples

axis_tolerance_deg._reason: a coast segment within this of horizontal or vertical (parallel to a map edge) counts toward axis_share, reported by the survey (it does not tell a straight coast from a wavy one: the old generator's wiggles scored as many aligned segments as a natural coast, so the floors are on spread and fill)

min_coast_spread._reason: FLOOR AGAINST A SQUARE OF LAND, per seed: the shore's spread (sqrt of the minor over the major variance of its points: how far it leaves one straight line, coast_stats().spread) is at least this. The first generator (a straight falloff from an edge) scored 0.06 to 0.10 on twelve seeds; this one 0.16 to 0.66 (an L, a bay, a peninsula or a scatter of islands scores 0.3 and up)

min_median_coast_spread._reason: and the median over the test's seeds at least this (the first generator's was 0.08)

max_land_fill._reason: the mainland (the land that reaches the map border) fills at most this share of its bounding box, per seed: a square block of land fills nearly all of it

max_median_land_fill._reason: and the median over the test's seeds at most this (the first generator's was 0.93, this one's 0.85)

min_archetypes._reason: the test's twelve seeds make at least this many different shapes

min_share_spread._reason: and their sea shares differ by at least this much between the least and the most sea

min_coast_m._reason: every seed with a sea has at least this much coast (a map edge is 5,000 m: a straight coast along one has about that)

step_from_m._reason: where each depth step begins, as metres of depth below sea level: shallows 0 to 6, shelf 6 to 18, deep beyond. The boundaries sit roughly midway between the steps' own depths (-3, -10, -30 m) on a geometric scale, as the land's thresholds sit between its levels

heights_m._reason: Alex: 'Sounds good' to the lead's proposal of -3, -10 and -30 m: shallows, shelf, deep. The water SURFACE is flat at sea level (z = 0), so a shadow falls on it exactly as on level 0 land; these heights are the seabed's, they colour the wash and name the steps

names._reason: Alex: three steps, shallows / shelf / deep

enabled._reason: the river is made unless this is off (a test knob)

min_m._reason: the river crosses the road at least this far from the village's centre (along the straight line), so the village is not on the bank; the board's river frame shows the road, the bank and the village together

max_m._reason: and at most this far; the road is about 1,700 m long

map_margin_m._reason: the crossing lies at least this far inside the map edge

cliff_clear_m._reason: and this far from a height boundary: the river meets the road on low ground

battery_gap_m._reason: and this far from either anti-aircraft battery

waypoint_m._reason: the river runs square across the road: it is routed through points this far either side of the crossing, along the road's normal

exempt_m._reason: the road within this of the crossing may be wet; every other point of the road stays dry

gap_max_m._reason: but the wet stretch of the road at the crossing (the gap where a bridge will go) is at most this long: a river that runs along the road for 100 m is not a crossing

length_max_m._reason: a course longer than this winds round the keep-out areas like a moat; another crossing is tried instead

length_good_m._reason: the search keeps the SHORTEST valid course; one this short ends it

tries._reason: crossing points tried (a seeded order) before the seed has a river that does not cross the road, or none

step_m._reason: the coarse grid the river is routed on (126 x 126 over the map); the route is then rounded and given meanders

upland_weight._reason: cost multiplier on high ground (the terrain field at or above the first threshold less a margin): a river does not climb a scarp

low_weight._reason: cost added by landness: the route prefers low ground, so it runs down the valley the large-scale field makes

wiggle._reason: cost = 1 + this x noise per cell, so no two rivers run alike

wiggle_noise_per_cell._reason: the frequency of that noise per cell

village_gap_m._reason: no route cell nearer than this to the village's outline

road_corridor_m._reason: cells this close to the road (away from the crossing) cost road_weight times more, so the river does not run along it

min_m._reason: the spring is at least this far (straight line) upstream of the crossing

foot_band._reason: a spring rises at the foot of high ground: where the terrain field is between 0.04 and 0.005 under the first threshold (low ground just beside an upland)

candidates._reason: springs routed to, the cheapest route wins

depth_m._reason: the river ends where the sea is this deep, and runs on a little way into it

goals._reason: sea cells routed to, the nearest to the crossing first

smooth_passes._reason: Chaikin passes over the routed polyline (the prototype's way of turning a polyline into a hand-drawn curve)

sample_m._reason: the spacing of the river's vertices

meander_m._reason: amplitude of the sideways meander, from the spring to the mouth

meander_taper_m._reason: no meander within this of the crossing, so the river meets the road square

source_taper_m._reason: nor within this of the spring

half_width_m._reason: half width from the spring to the mouth (a brook of 5 m to an estuary of 52 m)

half_width_power._reason: half width = lerp(first, last, u), u = (distance from the spring / the distance at which the width reaches the crossing width) ^ this

crossing_half_width_m._reason: half width where the river crosses the road, wherever that is along its course (26 m: the span a bridge will have to cover); it widens to the last of half_width_m further down

centre_depth_m._reason: depth in the middle, from the spring to the mouth; the section is a parabola, so a brook is shallows all through, and the lower river has a shelf in its middle

centre_depth_power._reason: centre depth = lerp(first, last, u ^ this), u as for the width: a wider river is a deeper one

sites._about: THE SIMULATION'S WATER SITES (Track WS, 2026-10-10; scripts/world/water_sites.gd and WaterGen.sites() make them, a scenario names them: 'water.bridge', 'water.patrol_loop', 'water.supply_route'). What is ALEX'S (decisions water-layer, boat-looks, bridge-look): the bridge where the road crosses the river; an armed patrol boat and an unarmed supply boat that are part of the environment with real patrols and no part in the mission; boats at the planes' scale, so they keep to the coast and the estuary, not up the river. EVERYTHING BELOW IS PROPOSED by Track WS. The sites are a pure function of the seed (and these records): a clearance grid over the map (the distance from each patch of open water to the nearest shore, shoal or map edge), a patrol LOOP fitted to it nearest the river's mouth (or, with no river, the village), and a SUPPLY ROUTE from the coast nearest the mouth to the farthest coast (the mainland's or an island's) the water reaches within a trip's length. Every site is checked against the exact water query (WaterGen.depth_at), not the grid alone.

grid_m._reason: the clearance grid's cell: 83 x 83 samples over the inset map; the loops and routes are then checked exactly, so the grid only has to be fine enough to find room

grid_slack_m._reason: the clearance grid is only good to about half a cell (it cannot see a shoal between two cells, and its distances are a chamfer's): a place passes the grid with this much more clearance than the margin the exact check will ask of it, so the exact check is not failed over a sliver

map_inset_m._reason: a boat's loop and route stay this far inside the map's edge (the map edge is an artificial shore): the units stay on the map, and a boat that is turning has room

nav_depth_m._reason: open water is water at least this deep: a metre under the deepest keel at least (data/units: patrol_boat draught 2.0 m, supply_boat 1.8 m) and half the generator's first step (the shallows, 0 to 6 m), so boats keep to the water the generator draws as more than a wash of shallows

sample_m._reason: a loop or a route is checked every this many metres along its legs

tangent_m._reason: the road's heading at the crossing is the direction from this far before the crossing to this far after it (the road is sampled every 10 m and wanders a little)

margin_m._reason: every point of the loop is at least this far from the shore, a shoal shallower than nav_depth_m and the map's inset edge: the boat is 27 m long and turns in a circle 114 m across at cruise, but at the corners of the loop it cuts inside the rectangle, and it strays under 20 m from it; the loop hugs the coast at this distance rather than lying out in the deep

half_width_m._reason: the loop is a rectangle, its long legs run along the coast this far either side of its axis (240 m across): wide enough that a boat turning at 10 deg/s (a 57 m radius) rounds the corners without a figure of eight

half_lengths_m._reason: half the length of the loop, tried longest first at each spot (900, 700, 520 and 380 m long): the loop is the longest that fits at the first place that has room; at 10 m/s a lap of the longest is about forty turns, of the shortest (as seed 20261009's) about twenty-five

orientation_step_deg._reason: the loop's direction is tried every this many degrees, starting from along the coast and fanning out

tangent_span_deg._reason: where the coast's direction can be told (the clearance falls toward a shore) only orientations within this of it are tried: the loop runs along the coast, not into it. In open water, where there is no coast to run along, every direction is tried

max_candidates._reason: centres tried, nearest the river's mouth first, before the seed is given no patrol loop (and starts, for the supply route, before it is given no route)

margin_m._reason: every point of the route is at least this far from the shore, a shoal and the inset edge: room for the barge to swing round at either end of its shuttle (a turn back at 5 m/s is a circle 114 m across, so the boat strays up to 114 m off the route there) with its 34 m hull and a margin to spare

length_m._reason: the route runs up to this far (by water) from its first point, the anchorage nearest the river's mouth, if the water allows: at 5 m/s a one-way trip is about 36 turns, so in the strike's twenty turns the barge is under way, not at its berth

min_length_m._reason: a shorter route than this is no route: the seed has no supply boat

loop_gap_m._reason: the supply route keeps at least this far from the patrol loop (the nearest point of its rectangle), its first point and every cell of its way: the two boats do not start on top of each other and the barge does not sail through the patrol's beat

coast_slack_m._reason: the route's far end HUGS THE COAST: its distance from the real shore (a shoal, an island, the land; not the map's inset edge) is at most the margin plus this plus coast_tolerance_m, so a barge works the shore and does not wander out to the deep

coast_tolerance_m._reason: how far past margin plus coast_slack_m a cell may be from the shore and still hug it: the clearance grid is 50 m a cell

simplify_m._reason: the way by water is a chain of grid cells; it is straightened (Douglas-Peucker) to a few waypoints, no leg of which strays this far from the chain, and each leg is checked exactly: a leg that fails the check is split again

tries._reason: ends tried from one start, the best hugging the coast first, before the next start is tried

start_tries._reason: starts tried (the open cells nearest the river's mouth that are clear of the patrol loop and have a way of min_length_m) before the seed is given no supply route

village_margin_m._reason: the village's outline grown by this must stay dry (the village's own polygon already has room round its houses)

tower_ring_m._reason: a ring this far round the radio tower's site (its compound)

battery_ring_m._reason: a ring this far round each battery site (the layout wants 25 m of open ground round it)

sample_m._reason: spacing of the sample points inside a keep-dry area

road_sample_m._reason: spacing of the road's points that must stay dry (except at the crossing)

px_per_m._reason: the board draws at the map's scale (data/terrain/terrain.json scale.px_per_m, the demo baseline)

grid_cell_m._reason: the sea's contour grid, as the terrain's (chunks.cell_m); rivers are not on it (they are drawn as ribbons: an 8 m grid cannot hold a 5 m brook)

hue_deg._reason: Alex 2026-10-10: 'Hue 222, the first'. The water's hue (OKLCH). 20 degrees from the shadow tint (steel, 242) and 38 from the slate-blue side accent (side_b, 260), so the three blues are three blues and not one; the board shows it beside teal (200) and the shadow's own hue (242)

lightness_below_paper._reason: L of each depth step = the paper's L less this (paper 0.847): shallows 0.817, shelf 0.737, deep 0.647. Lightness is the ramp off paper, darker with depth, the way the land lifts from paper with height. The deep step stays well above the shadow tint (0.513) so a shadow still reads on it, and above the slate accent (0.551) so the enemy's colour is the darker thing

chroma._reason: more saturated with depth (Alex), and always under the shadow tint's 0.076 and the accents' 0.100: water is the quietest blue in the drawing

wash_alpha._reason: alpha of the wash; the paper's own mottle shows through by paper_mottle instead

paper_mottle._reason: how much of the paper tint's variation (the paper shader's low-frequency mottle, +/- 5 percent) the wash keeps, so water looks like a wash on paper and not a flat digital fill

halo_lift._reason: L added to the land at the water's edge in the soft options (C, E): the reference's pale band. Lightness off paper, no new hue

halo_chroma_scale._reason: chroma of the pale band as a fraction of the paper's (it eases down as it lightens, like the land's level fills)

ink_weight._reason: named multiplier from render_defaults.json linework: the shoreline is an edge like a scarp's contour (1.15)

step_weight._reason: named multiplier: a depth step is a fainter line than the shore (0.8)

step_alphas._reason: alpha of the line at each step's top (the shore, the shelf's edge, the deep's edge): fading with depth like the land's nested contours (0.9, 0.6, 0.4)

pale_alpha._reason: alpha of option F's pale step edge (paper-coloured, lifted)

pale_lift._reason: L added to the step above for option F's pale edge

pale_width_px._reason: option F's pale edge width at zoom 1 (scaled by the zoom, not below 1 px)

blur_m._reason: gaussian sigma of the sea shore's soft edge (C, E), in metres: the shallows melt into the ground over about 3 sigma = 33 m

river_blur_m._reason: sigma of a river's soft edge: a 26 m river keeps a readable bank (a blur as wide as the sea's would wipe it out)

river_halo_m._reason: sigma of the pale band along a river bank

halo_m._reason: sigma of the pale band on the land (C, E)

gradient_blur_m._reason: option E's smooth gradient is the same three masks blurred by these sigmas (shore, shelf edge, deep edge), so the steps run into one another

offsets_m._reason: option D: water-lining, ink lines this far from the shore into the water

alphas._reason: fading with distance (hairlines at the planning zoom lose alpha with width, so these start strong)

weight._reason: named multiplier: the lightest ink line that is not a hatch (0.75)

break_noise_per_px._reason: the prototype's pen-lift noise (rut lines 0.045 per 3 px)

break_threshold._reason: per line: a line lifts the pen where the noise is under this, so the outer lines are more broken (dashes)

working_default._reason: Alex 2026-10-10 on variants/water/: 'A · Ink line at each step'

A.title: Stepped wash, an ink line at each depth step

B.title: Stepped wash, no step lines, an inked shoreline

C.title: Stepped wash, a soft shore and a pale band on the land

D.title: Stepped wash, ink ripple lines along the shore

E.title: A smooth gradient (the reference's way), for comparison

F.title: Stepped wash, pale step edges and no ink on the water

options._reason: A to E are the lead's list; F is the one more Track WB suggests: the steps are divided by a thin PAPER-coloured line instead of ink (the white rim of a hand-coloured chart), so nothing dark competes with the planes' ink outlines or the enemy accent on the water, and the shore is the wash's own edge. Each option is a few switches; the drawing reads them from here

palette_variants._reason: the board's palette row re-renders the coast and the markers at these hues with the working default option; the question is how the water blue sits beside the shadow tint (242) and the slate-blue accent (260)
